title: Counterweight Loft
provenance: Original Postern rehearsal authored 27 September 2026. Fictional mechanisms; not Wrenmere canon. Difficulty is not human-calibrated.

intro.storyOn: At the top of the service stair, a platform hangs between two pans. A small tool compartment moves with it. The latch can hold a balanced platform, but balancing and latching are not the same action.
intro.storyOff: Balance the platform, engage its latch and recover the hatch tool. One fixed unit is already on the left pan. Movable weights 1, 3, 4, 5 must all be deployed for the latch to engage.

ending.storyOn: The platform stays on its latch while the hatch tool turns. You reused a recovered resource without confusing a temporary balance with a persistent mechanical state.
ending.storyOff: The platform stays on its latch while the hatch tool turns. You reused a recovered resource without confusing a temporary balance with a persistent mechanical state.

solution.storyOn: The total is 14 including the fixed left unit, so each pan needs 7. Put movable 1 and 5 on the left; put 3 and 4 on the right. Engage the latch. Take the tool from the revealed compartment and fit it to the hatch, then open the hatch. The latch holds even if weights move later; none is consumed.
solution.storyOff: The total is 14 including the fixed left unit, so each pan needs 7. Put movable 1 and 5 on the left; put 3 and 4 on the right. Engage the latch. Take the tool from the revealed compartment and fit it to the hatch, then open the hatch. The latch holds even if weights move later; none is consumed.

text.storyOn: The left pan carries a fixed unit of 1. Movable weights are 1, 3, 4, 5. With every movable weight off the shelf, equal pan totals let the latch engage. Once engaged, the latch supports the platform independently of the weights.
text.storyOff: The left pan carries a fixed unit of 1. Movable weights are 1, 3, 4, 5. With every movable weight off the shelf, equal pan totals let the latch engage. Once engaged, the latch supports the platform independently of the weights.
